name: Monastic Sign Language
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.note: Catalogue record only: classification under Sign Language (auxiliary sign systems), ISO mzg, refs Barakat 1975 and Quay 2015.

Nothing. Secondary encyclopedia page: describes monastic sign systems as manual/gestural sign lexicons ('better understood as forms of symbolic gestural communication rather than languages'; 'No grammar is described for these signs, and they were probably used in the word order of an oral language'). No spoken form, hence no word stress. Bibliography names Barakat 1975, Umiker-Sebeok & Sebeok 1987, Bruce 2007, Quay 2001, Kendon 1990, Stokoe 1978.

sources.citation: Quay, Suzanne. 2015. Monastic sign language from medieval to modern times. In Jepsen et al. (eds.), Sign Languages of the World: A Comparative Handbook, 871-900. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
